The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has challenged members of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council and the Rainbow Coalition to ensure that opposition parties do not secure 25 per cent of the votes in the FCT in the January 16, 2027 general election. Wike specifically mentioned the African Democratic Congress and the Nigeria Democratic Congress, urging the campaign council to intensify grassroots mobilisation and take the achievements of President Bola Tinubu’s administration to voters across the six area councils. According to a statement issued by the Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media to the Minister, Lere Olayinka, Wike spoke on Monday in Abuja during the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council/Rainbow Coalition FCT at the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre. Wike, who is the coordinator of the FCT Presidential Campaign Council, said members must not take victory for granted but should use the administration’s record in infrastructure development and institutional reforms as the basis of their campaign. He urged them to focus on presenting verifiable achievements rather than engaging in political rhetoric. “You don’t need to go and see a prophet. You don’t need to go and see any doctor or anybody to tell you what to do. It is obvious; it is factual. Look at what Mr President has done for the people of the FCT. These are the tools you need to campaign,” Wike said. The minister argued that Tinubu had demonstrated commitment to the development of the FCT and the political inclusion of its residents, particularly through reforms addressing longstanding demands of the territory. He said 50 years after Abuja was created in 1976, Tinubu became the first President to ensure that the FCT was represented at the Federal Executive Council, where major national policies and decisions are taken. Wike also cited the creation of the Mandate Secretariats for Women Affairs and Youth Development, saying they had provided opportunities for women and young people to participate more actively in governance. On the financial autonomy of the territory, he said the removal of the FCT from the Treasury Single Account arrangement had enabled it to access loans to finance critical infrastructure projects. The minister also challenged opposition politicians to compare infrastructure projects executed by previous administrations with those delivered since Tinubu assumed office in 2023. He particularly highlighted the administration’s record in issuing Certificates of Occupancy, claiming that successive governments between 1999 and 2023 issued about 7,000 to 8,000 certificates, compared with more than 20,000 issued by the Tinubu administration within three years. How?” he queried. Wike urged members of the campaign council to take the message to communities, wards and polling units, particularly in satellite towns, where residents could assess the impact of government projects. Earlier, the FCT Chairman of the APC, Ishaku Tanko Yamawo, expressed confidence in the party’s ability to mobilise support for Tinubu and its National Assembly candidates in the forthcoming elections. Yamawo said the infrastructure projects executed under Wike’s leadership had become a major part of the party’s campaign message. “Your projects have already become our strongest campaign message. The goodwill and confidence you have earned among our people, both indigenes and residents of the FCT, are exceptional,” he told the minister. He commended the Rainbow Coalition for bringing different political interests together, saying the alliance would strengthen the party’s mobilisation across the six area councils. Yamawo urged members of the campaign council to work together, maintain effective coordination and ensure that the APC’s message reached every ward and polling unit. Also speaking, the FCT Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Ismaila Mohammed Dogara, expressed confidence in the ability of political leaders and stakeholders within the Rainbow Coalition to mobilise support for Tinubu and other endorsed candidates. Dogara commended Wike for building a political structure capable of sustaining mobilisation and coordinating electoral activities even in the minister’s absence. He said the cooperation between APC and PDP leaders under the coalition demonstrated their readiness to work together towards the forthcoming elections. “Even if you are not in the FCT, our executive chairman does not allow any space, not even for one minute, before taking it from where you stopped. That shows that on the fateful day of the election, if the Honourable Minister is not in the FCT, those leaders are ready and capable of delivering, Mr President, Senator Philip Aduda, Tanimu and others,” Dogara said. He expressed optimism that members of the coalition would return to the conference centre on January 17, a day after the election, to celebrate their anticipated victory. “The big day is January 16, and the return day is January 17. By the special grace of God, we are going to return to this hall to celebrate,” he declared.
